Here is the issue:
Issue Title: [FEATURE] Expose input messages to BeforeInvocationEvent hook

Description:
### Problem Statement

To implement standalone input-side guardrails (for e.g. PII, toxic content, prompt attack prevention), we'd like to place a Hook as early as possible in the invocation. In particular, we want to make sure it runs (and has the opportunity to redact the user's input message) before the message gets added to memory by e.g. AgentCoreMemorySessionManager, which [hooks on](https://github.com/aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python/blob/eee67daee92d10bba137d30594694444c40f1635/src/bedrock_agentcore/memory/integrations/strands/session_manager.py#L544) `MessageAddedEvent`.

However, the current `BeforeInvocationEvent` hook only [receives](https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python/blob/2a26ffad8bc7379358bc2535d9ce1ec290fea0af/src/strands/agent/agent.py#L609) a reference to the agent and has no visibility of the incoming `messages` because they haven't been added to `agent.messages` yet.

### Proposed Solution

Extend `BeforeInvocationEvent` to also include the `messages` received during `_run_loop()` start-up
- The simplest implementation of this would implicitly allow hook authors to edit the messages in-place, giving them the opportunity to redact the message but go ahead with the invocation. 👍
- A guardrail hook could also choose to just raise error and abort the whole agent invocation, which could save some money in cases where the manner of redaction leaves nothing useful the agent could do (see also #758)

In `structured_output_async()`, this event is also currently [raised](https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python/blob/2a26ffad8bc7379358bc2535d9ce1ec290fea0af/src/strands/agent/agent.py#L487) but **before** `agent.messages` and the optional `prompt` argument have been combined to form the `temp_messages` that'll ultimately be used in the invocation.
- AFAICT there's nothing stateful about the [construction of temp_messages](https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python/blob/2a26ffad8bc7379358bc2535d9ce1ec290fea0af/src/strands/agent/agent.py#L495) and its only failure modes seem to be for malformed inputs - so I'd suggest to move the invocation of the BeforeInvocationEvent hooks to straight after `temp_messages` is set up.
- Specifically, I'd suggest to pull `temp_messages` and the `if not self.messages and not prompt` guard clause **forward** out of the tracing span - treating them as input validation activities that don't count towards the span duration (negligible anyway) but also wouldn't trigger `AfterInvocationEvent` in case they fail due to malformed input.

### Use Case

As mentioned above, primary use-case here is for input guardrail checks to prevent PII / toxic / prompt-attack content from entering the agent as early as possible in the invocation lifecycle.

### Alternatives Solutions

Today I think the next-earliest workaround is for an input guardrail to hook on to `MessageAddedEvent` instead (since this'll get called as soon as the agent initializes its messages list, *before* `BeforeModelCallEvent`)... But this is not ideal because MessageAdded is a typical place for session/memory managers (like AgentCoreMemorySessionManager) to hook - so relies on users to connect their guardrail and memory hooks in the right sequence to avoid leakage of sensitive/malicious input into memory. It should work, but is easy to mis-configure without realizing.

### Additional Context

_No response_
